name: Light Violet
lede: Light Violet is a soft blue-violet whose name has meant different colors on different charts; on one survey it is a pale pink-lilac instead.

sections.title: A name that moves
sections.body: The library holds two quite different colors under this name: the Ridgway and ISCC-NBS bluish tint shown here, and the xkcd survey's much lighter, pinker #D6B4FC [1]. Names this plain get stretched. A seventeenth-century merchant quoted by Balfour-Paul described good indigo as giving off a pure light violet vapour when burned [2]. Gurney, a painter, uses the words for sky blue bouncing off a red surface [3]. Neither points at one fixed color.

sections.title: On the old charts
sections.body: Ridgway's 1912 atlas shows it on plate X, and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system files it in blocks 195 and 206, where its other names include Bluish Violet and Lavender-Violet [1]. The nearest everyday name is [[periwinkle]], about eight units away; neighbors are [[violet]], [[lavender-violet]] and [[lilac]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Only 2 of 23,781 museum paintings contain the swatch, about 0.01 per cent, rarer than 86 per cent of our named colors [4]. In printed English the phrase's word peaks in the 1930s [4].
